message:
fix(host): guard the preview budget -- Serve runs on two threads, not one

Product 1, test 0, build 0. Fixes a race introduced one commit ago in 93deceb.

The budget went in as a bare function-local static under a comment saying the control dispatcher
is one per process and therefore only one thread ever touches it. That is wrong, and the
reviewer's incident note is what prompted checking it. With controlPort > 0 the host starts two
threads on the SAME ControlSessionServer -- the TCP controlThread (host_startup_control.cpp:127,
serving at :163) and the UDP udpControlThread (:397, serving at :431) -- and an operational host
runs both, which its own log shows as "control waiting port=43001" beside "udp bound port=43000".

So two threads would have been inserting into the same unordered_map. Not a theoretical window
either: a picker open on one transport while the other is connected is an ordinary afternoon.

The map is now under a mutex, and the capture deliberately is not. Holding the budget across a
call that may run for a full deadline would make one dispatcher wait on the other's helper, which
would hand back a smaller version of the problem this whole change is about.

The same correction applies to something written down earlier in this task: the design note said
concurrency could be capped at one because thumbnails are structurally serial. They are serial
PER DISPATCHER. With two, at most two helpers are alive at once -- which is within the bound the
task allowed, but it is two rather than one, and the comment now says so where the assumption
lives instead of in a message.
